fields.options:
Add this to your Print Format's HTML. Leave Anchor Text above at its default - the same value works for every template regardless of size, since size lives entirely in the HTML, not here:

<div style="display:inline-block; position:relative; width:160px; height:80px; margin:4px 0;">
  <span style="color:#ffffff; position:absolute; left:0; top:0;">##DIGITAL_SIGN_ANCHOR:160x80##</span>
</div>

The :WxH suffix in the HTML above is optional and detected automatically from what's actually rendered - add it only in the Print Format's HTML to size that particular template. Leaving it off entirely (plain ##DIGITAL_SIGN_ANCHOR##) falls back to 160x80 automatically. Keep the div's own width/height matching whatever number you use in the anchor text - the div reserves the layout space so the stamp doesn't overlap surrounding content, and the anchor text tells the signing code how big to actually draw the stamp; if the two disagree, the stamp will be sized correctly but may not fit the space reserved for it.

160x80 is a reasonable default with every stamp field enabled (signer/reason/location/date/certificate serial - up to 5 lines of text).

The stamp is drawn extending downward-right from exactly where the anchor text sits, so position:absolute; left:0; top:0; matters: it pins the anchor to the reserved box's own top-left corner, so the stamp fills downward into that box instead of needing space reserved above it (some PDF engines don't reliably reserve space above an anchor sitting right after a line of text, which caused overlap with earlier top:0-less or bottom:0 anchors). The stamp content is centered (both directions) within that box automatically.

Use color:#ffffff (matching the background), not opacity:0 - some PDF engines skip painting opacity:0 text entirely, dropping it from the searchable text layer too. If the surrounding background isn't white, match this color to it instead.
